about: Curated open class action settlements and FTC refund programs (cluster K12, C90). Owner's sourcing law: no official registry of open settlements exists, so rows come from two tiers only — Tier 1 government (the FTC refunds chart at ftc.gov/enforcement/refunds, FTC/state AG releases, CFPB/SEC lists) and Tier 2 court-appointed administrators (Kroll, JND, Epiq, Angeion, Rust, Simpluris, Analytics, CPT) verified against the court docket. Aggregators were discovery-only and are never a row's source. Every row carries its source URL, court/docket, administrator, claim deadline and the date it was checked. A row that cannot be verified does not ship. Re-check monthly; past fresh_days a row is said to may have changed. Upmore prepares claim packets; the owner files — filing is the owner's legal tap, never the agent's.

settlements.case_name: Kingsbury, et al. v. Evernorth Health Inc., et al.
settlements.checked_how: Read on the court-authorized settlement website itself (ehisettlement.com) on 2026-10-12; deadline and payout cross-checked against the administrator's claim materials the same day.
settlements.court: Circuit Court for the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit, Hillsborough County, Florida
settlements.eligibility: You signed in to MDLIVE's portal at patient.mdlive.com and did anything in the portal after signing in between May 30, 2023 and August 11, 2025, and you had an active Facebook and/or Google account during that time. The online claim form opens with the Claimant ID from your notice, and you attest to the portal use on the form.
settlements.name: MDLIVE / Evernorth privacy settlement
settlements.payout_summary: Up to $15.00 cash, reduced pro rata if valid claims exceed the cap
settlements.proof_required: Claimant ID from the notice, plus the sworn attestation on the claim form. No receipts.
settlements.summary: The suit alleges MDLIVE's patient portal shared users' sensitive information and private communications with Google and Meta without consent. The defendants deny the allegations. The settlement pays all valid claims, notice and administration costs, fees and service awards up to a $3,500,000 cap.

settlements.case_name: Cooper v. Telmate, LLC d/b/a ViaPath Technologies
settlements.checked_how: Read on the court-authorized settlement website itself (telmatedatabreachsettlement.com) on 2026-10-12; case caption and docket from the statement issued by Kroll Settlement Administration LLC about the case.
settlements.court: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia
settlements.eligibility: Your personal information was impacted in the August 2020 Telmate security incident — in practice, you received a notice about it. Class members can claim a pro rata cash payment with no documentation, and/or reimbursement of documented out-of-pocket losses up to $5,000 with proof.
settlements.name: Telmate data breach settlement
settlements.payout_summary: A pro rata cash payment (amount set by how many valid claims are filed), plus documented out-of-pocket losses up to $5,000
settlements.proof_required: None for the pro rata cash payment. Receipts or statements for a documented-loss claim (up to $5,000).
settlements.summary: A data breach between August 11 and August 13, 2020 exposed the personal information of people who used Telmate's services (such as GettingOut and VisitNow). Telmate denies all allegations. The settlement fund is $4,225,000.

settlements.case_name: In re: Kelly Benefits Data Breach Litigation
settlements.checked_how: Caption and docket read from the court's own memorandum in the case (Case 1:25-cv-01304-SAG, D. Md., on govinfo.gov); administrator, deadline, fund and benefits as stated in the settlement's claim materials naming Kelly Benefits Data Breach Litigation, c/o Kroll Settlement Administration LLC. The settlement website itself refused this reader's fetch on 2026-10-12 (HTTP 403), so the site's own text was not re-read that day.
settlements.court: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland
settlements.eligibility: You are a United States resident whose private information was compromised in the December 2024 Kelly Benefits data breach — in practice, you received a notice. Filing online takes the Class Member ID from the notice. Class members with a California address on December 12, 2024 can also claim a statutory payment estimated at $100.
settlements.name: Kelly Benefits data breach settlement
settlements.payout_summary: A pro rata cash payment estimated at $50, documented out-of-pocket losses up to $5,000, and three years of credit monitoring if you elect it
settlements.proof_required: Class Member ID from the notice to file online. Documentation (statements, receipts) only for a documented-loss claim.
settlements.summary: Attackers accessed Kelly Benefits' systems between December 12 and December 17, 2024 and copied files with names, Social Security numbers, tax IDs, dates of birth, medical and health insurance information and financial account information. Kelly Benefits denies wrongdoing. The settlement fund is $5,000,000.

settlements.administrator: Amazon, under FTC order (no claim administrator; the FTC lists no claims contact because no claim is filed)
settlements.case_name: Federal Trade Commission v. Amazon (Prime enrollment and cancellation)
settlements.checked_how: The FTC's own refunds chart (ftc.gov/enforcement/refunds) read on 2026-10-12 lists 'Amazon Refunds' among its active refund programs (September 2026). Program terms as the FTC states them: payments are automatic — nobody files a claim.
settlements.docket: Listed on the FTC refunds chart, checked 2026-10-12
settlements.eligibility: A U.S. Amazon Prime member who enrolled through the challenged sign-up flow, or tried to cancel online and could not, between June 23, 2019 and June 23, 2025, and used no more than 20 Prime benefits in a 12-month period after enrolling. There is no claim form; the FTC is not calling, texting or emailing anyone about this refund, and anyone who asks you for money or account details to release it is running a scam.
settlements.name: Amazon Prime refunds (FTC)
settlements.payout_summary: Automatic refunds up to $51 in the first rounds; expanded payments from October 1, 2026 can bring the total to up to $200 per person
settlements.proof_required: None — there is no claim to file. Payments are automatic.
settlements.summary: The FTC's case over Prime enrollment and cancellation flows. Refunds are sent automatically by check, PayPal or Venmo to people who qualify; earlier recipients got up to $51, and expanded automatic payments that began October 1, 2026 can bring a person's total to up to $200, with a further eligibility assessment in February 2027. Payments expire 60 days after they are issued.
